title: Lead-exposure exception uses a later national cut-off
summary: The current exception uses 16 May rather than 9 April 2026. Its scope could include additional historic lead exposure; no affected worker has been identified.
nationalGap: Regulation 49/2026 §13(5) instead refers to exposure before its own commencement, 16 May 2026. This extends the express qualifying period by 37 days.
consequence: Exposure during 9 April–15 May could qualify for continued work above the ordinary blood limit. Actual eligibility and any practical effect remain unverified.
resolution: The official current-version API still returns the original operative version, without an end date. No later correction was located.
caveat: The national rule retains initial work suspension, regular medical surveillance, the upper 70µg/100 ml threshold and a declining blood-lead trend. General prevention duties and directive-consistent interpretation remain relevant. This is a conditional scope comparison, not evidence of an unsafe workplace.
review: Two agents independently read the authentic EU exception and current national §13. Qualified concern; no worker-level outcome assessed.

comparison.note: Only the cut-off differs in this comparison; other safeguards remain.

recognitionNote: Bounded Estonian and English searches on 26 October 2026 combined lead, both dates, the national provision and incompatibility terms. Public consultation material described the new regime; no precise published comparison of these cut-offs was located. This does not establish first discovery.
